title: edgecase-quant-debug-scratchpad
content:
Notes to self - messy timeline + commands + hypotheses for BF16/INT8 NaN regressions

Context:
- Running local repros for customer X where we see occasional NaNs when switching to INT8 weights with BF16 activations. Hosted infra sometimes falls back and recovers; dedicated private runs more deterministic.
- Models affected: 13B and 70B family variants, primarily after recent kernel selector change that enables fused rotary+layernorm fastpath.
- Symptoms: generation produces `nan` tokens mid-sequence (softmax/ln outputs become NaN), or logits go to ±inf. Not always reproducible; seems data-dependent (long prefixes, dense attention).

Quick reproduction commands I used (local docker dev):
- Quantize (per-channel symmetric, calibration 256 samples):
  python tools/quantize_model.py \\n    --model-dir ./models/mymodel-13b \\n    --out ./tmp/q_mymodel-13b_int8 \\n    --backend perchannel-symmetric \\n    --dtype int8 \\n    --calib-samples 256 \\n    --calib-dataset ../calib/prompt-snippets.txt

- Run local inference loop (single GPU):
  python serve_local.py \\n    --model ./tmp/q_mymodel-13b_int8 \\n    --dtype bf16 \\n    --max-seq-len 1024 \\n    --batch-size 1 \\n    --warmup 10 \\n    --log-level debug \\
    --dump-tensors /tmp/dumps

- Quick gradient-free check (no grad):
  CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python tests/run_infer_debug.py --model ... --profile-kernels

Observed error snippets (copied raw):
- mid-run crash in hosted logs: `RuntimeError: cuDNN error: CUDNN_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` (we later think it's mask mismatch rather than cudnn)
- generator output: `NaN detected in logits at step 37: token 4632`
- local dump: first NaN appears in attn_scores before softmax: `tensor([nan, nan, ...], device='cuda:0')`
- kernel-level: `CUDA error: device-side assert triggered` (usually from indexing bug)

Immediate checks I ran:
- Sanity: run full-fp32 and BF16 (no weight quant) with same prompts -> no NaNs.
- Run INT8 weights + FP32 activations -> generally OK.
- INT8 weights + BF16 activations -> NaNs show up. Suggests interaction BF16 activation path + quantized weight math.
- Compare attention mask shapes in failing prompts vs passing ones -> failing case had large trailing padding (seq len mismatch) causing some broadcast to shape mismatch in fused kernel.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel math / fused op numerical instability: fused rotary + layernorm implementation uses BF16 fastpath with reduced accumulation precision that, when paired with INT8-dequant noise, pushes some denominators to zero in softmax.
2) Per-channel quant scales: some channels have extremely small scale -> large dequant values -> overflow in BF16 -> NaN. Need to clamp scales or use per-tensor for problematic layers.
3) Attention mask / sequence packing bug: wrong mask broadcast leads to -inf fed into softmax incorrectly (or all -inf if mask obtuse) -> NaN after subsequent ops.
4) KV-cache indexing bug in our runtime when quantized weights used (index rounding) -> device assert.

What to dump next (practical checklist):
- Add instrumentation to dump min/max/mean/std/zero_count for tensors at key points (weight dequant, linear output, pre-attn scores, softmax inputs, softmax outputs, ln inputs/outputs).
- For headers: print quant scales and zero points per-channel for each layer when loading quantized model. Save top-5 smallest scales (they are suspect).
- Re-run failing prompt with single-step dumps and small batch size.
- Try clamp tiny scales to epsilon=1e-4 and rerun.
- Run same quantized model but force activation dtype to fp32 and compare.

Commands I added to runtime for quick stats (cheat snippets):
- in runtime/ops/linear_kernel.cu (debug build): after dequant: cudaMemcpy host 1 elem; printf("L%d deq min %f max %f\n", layer, minf, maxf);
- in python serve_local.py add: --verify-quant-scales -> prints first/last 10 scales per layer.

Calibration notes (might be root cause):
- Calibration data skewed: used short prompts only. When long-context test runs, activations go out of calibration range -> scale mismatch. Need mixed-length calibration (include long tails).
- Observed some layers where min==max during calibration (flat activations) -> quantizer produced scale=0 or near-zero -> later dequant multiply by huge. Fix by forcing floor on scale.

Experiments tried and quick results:
- Per-channel symmetric -> FAIL (NaNs)
- Per-tensor asymmetric -> REDUCED NaNs but worse perplexity in some prompts
- Keep final layer(s) FP32 (no quant) -> PASS (suggests last layers sensitive)
- Clamp scales to 1e-3 globally -> PASS on failing prompt but increases RMSE vs fp32 a lot; this is a bandaid.
- Disable fused rotary+layernorm fastpath -> PASS consistently. That implicates fused kernel.

Interim conclusion: The fused kernel + BF16 fastpath likely amplifies small quantization noise from INT8 weights; tiny per-channel scales (from bad calibration) are triggering large dequant values -> BF16 accumulation saturates/underflows producing NaN. Also mask shape issues occasionally make symptom worse.

Next steps / experiments to run (prioritized):
1) Reproduce deterministically: pick 3 failing prompts from hosted logs, run in docker with same seed/hardware, enable single-step dumps.
2) Add assertion in fused kernel: check for inf/nan inputs and abort with more helpful message + layer id.
3) Update quantizer to enforce min_scale = max(min_scale, 1e-4) and re-evaluate accuracy vs stability tradeoff.
4) Add mixed-length calibration routine (include lengths up to 1024, 2048 depending on model).
5) Benchmark enabling fp32 accum for the fused kernel (slower) vs stability improvement; try hybrid: fp32 accum only for layers with min_scale < threshold.
6) Check rotary implementation math order (sin/cos multiply order) in fused kernel vs reference; maybe reorder causes precision loss in BF16.

Notes for bug report to runtime team:
- Repro prompts: (shred list) provided in linked artifact GHD-2345
- Model hash: sha256: abcdef1234567890... (include exact one from failing hosted run)
- Environment: CUDA 12.2, drivers as on prod, cuDNN 8.7, PyTorch 2.2 nightly, custom runtime commit 0f4d3b2 (see PR 412)
- Observed when: INT8 weights + BF16 activations + fused rotary+ln fastpath ON + long padded sequences.

Open questions to discuss in sync with kernel owners:
- Is there an internal accumulation path for fused kernels that drops to BF16 early? Can we force fp32 accum?
- Should our quantizer bias-correct heavy-tail channels differently?
- Can runtime detect near-zero scales at load time and switch to per-tensor or fallback?

Random quick TODOs (personal):
- push minimal failing repro to github PR so CI can run (aim: reproducible in CI)
- add unit test for scale-clamping behavior in quantizer
- schedule 30m sync with @Avery Chen and @Maya Singh to decide mitigation

End of scratchpad. Will clean up and create a proper bug + mitigation doc after confirming deterministic repros.

-- Evan
